## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Double-anonymous. Manuscripts are admin-checked, allocated to an editor by subject specialism, who decides whether they merit double-anonymous review; the aim is three reviews from qualified scholars (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/european-journal-of-political-research/information/peer-review-information/review-process; retrieved 2026-11-23). The page says "one of our nine editors" while the board page lists 8 editor roles (1 editor-in-chief, 5 editors, 2 open-science editors) plus an editorial coordinator; the difference is not explained |
| **Transferable / Cascade?** | Blank. The review-process page read (2026-11-23) mentions no transfer scheme |
| **Reviewer reports published?** | Not as standard practice per anything read; the pages and the 2026 editorial mention none |
| **Typical R+R rounds** | The editors state that a granted revise-and-resubmit gives authors one chance at a major revision, after which the article will "either be (conditionally) accepted or rejected", and that a second decision of major revisions will be granted only "very exceptionally" (editorial, https://doi.org/10.1017/S1475676526101960, 2026-11-09). SciRev, n = 15: 1.7 rounds on average |
| **Reviewer recommendations** | Editors assess the general sentiment of the reviews; reaching revise-and-resubmit usually needs at least one positive set of comments; editors may override with strong reasons; reviewers are usually a mix of topical and methodological experts (editorial). Appeals are considered only for a significant factual error or a compromised process and are decided by the Editors with a team member not involved in the review (review-process page). Reviewer incivility is handled by a collective editor vote and a request to revise the comments (editorial) |

### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | Yes: a dedicated "Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) Tools" section in the author instructions, and a statement in the editors' 2026 editorial (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/european-journal-of-political-research/information/author-instructions/preparing-your-materials and https://doi.org/10.1017/S1475676526101960; retrieved 2026-11-23). On submission the corresponding author declares compliance with the Cambridge University Press AI contributions policy |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | No gate found. Use is allowed with transparent disclosure |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 (allowed with mandatory disclosure; the acknowledgements guidance warns that failure to acknowledge AI assistance "may lead to disqualification of the paper") |
| **Summary** | AI tools cannot be listed as authors. Declare and describe any use of an AI tool to generate text or images (translation included) or to analyse or extract insights from data; minimal non-generative uses (spelling or language checks, single words, minor formatting) need no declaration. The editors add that theory building, literature synthesis, research design and analytic conclusions "must originate from the human mind", that authors using AI must name the tools and purposes, and that reviewers must not upload unpublished manuscripts to public or commercial AI tools. Assistance from writing agencies, language editors or AI tools must also be noted in the cover letter and the Acknowledgements. Retrieved 2026-11-23 |
| **Source URL** | https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/european-journal-of-political-research/information/author-instructions/preparing-your-materials ; https://doi.org/10.1017/S1475676526101960 |

### Preprint Policy

> Journal-level statement: this journal "allows preprints to be posted anywhere at any time, including before submission to the journal" (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/european-journal-of-political-research/information/journal-policies/open-access-options, retrieved 2026-11-23). The prior-publication policy adds that a preprint on a personal website, institutional repository or preprint archive is not prior or duplicate publication (preparing-your-materials page). Review is double-anonymous, and the pages do not discuss whether a posted preprint conflicts with anonymity.

| Stage | Allowed? | Notes |
|-------|----------|-------|
| Pre-submission | Yes | Per the statements above |
| Under review | Yes | "At any time"; no separate under-review rule found |
| Post-acceptance (AAM) | Yes, conditions on the publisher page | The journal is fully Gold OA, so the accepted version is published openly; the Green OA spreadsheet the page links to was not read |
| Version of Record | Open access under a Creative Commons licence | Authors may choose any of the six CC licences (open-access-options page) |

## Format

> Source for the rules below: the journal's "Preparing your materials" page, https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/european-journal-of-political-research/information/author-instructions/preparing-your-materials (retrieved 2026-11-23), unless another page is named.

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | Research Article and Research Note (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/european-journal-of-political-research/information/instructions-contributors). Review articles do not qualify as research articles unless they present a substantive empirical contribution, "such as a systematic meta-analysis"; normative political theory is accepted when it contributes to and challenges key debates in empirical political science (preparing-your-materials page). A search-result snippet listed a "State-of-the-Field Review" type; the live instructions page does not |
| **Word limit** | Research Articles 10,000 words maximum and Research Notes 5,000, counting main text, footnotes, tables and figures but excluding references, abstract and appendices; over-length manuscripts "will be returned to authors: we do not make exceptions"; the limits apply to revised manuscripts as well (preparing-your-materials page) |
| **Word limit negotiability** | None offered: "we do not make exceptions" (same page) |
| **Abstract limit** | Abstract of up to 250 words and up to five keywords (preparing-your-materials page). Median abstract length among the 555 Crossref records that have one: 172 words, maximum 482 (computed 2026-11-23; the longest values may include extra text) |
| **Reference limit** | No cap found; references are excluded from the word count. Harvard author-date style (last name, year) in the text; initials rather than full first names; any consistent style is accepted at submission and Harvard is requested on acceptance |
| **Supplementary material** | Supplementary materials go in separate files (PDF or Word) and are shown to reviewers in the format submitted; they are published online with the article. Figures and tables not crucial to the argument, or longer than a page, may be published as supplementary material (preparing-your-materials page) |
| **Figure/Table limits** | No count limit found. Figures and tables are submitted on separate pages with their location indicated in the text (preparing-your-materials page) |
| **Style / submission format** | Page-numbered, double-spaced throughout including references, type size no smaller than 12 pt; British or American English consistently; ECPR house style; submission through ScholarOne at https://mc.manuscriptcentral.com/ejpr; title page with author names, affiliations and acknowledgments; funding and competing-interest statements required, an ethical-standards statement if human subjects are involved; ORCID required for the corresponding author (preparing-your-materials page) |

### Epistemological & Political Leanings

> Evidence layers: OpenAlex grouped counts over 610 works dated 2021-2026; Crossref records (591, 555 with abstract) for keyword counts; the editors' 2026 editorial (https://doi.org/10.1017/S1475676526101960) and the journal's aims text. Retrieved 2026-11-23.

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Cross-cultural friendliness** | Author countries on the 610 works dated 2021-2026 (OpenAlex; works with at least one author in the country): Germany 147 (24.1%), United Kingdom 130, Netherlands 73, Switzerland 71, United States 68, Denmark 61, Austria 51, Belgium 44, Norway 44, Italy 42, Sweden 42, Spain 37 (retrieved 2026-11-23). In the 2026 editorial the editors report that about half of 2025 submissions came from Western Europe and roughly 10% each from Northern Europe, Asia and North America, "strongly encourage" authors outside Western and Northern Europe to submit, and state that a single-country case alone "is not sufficient to pass the bar of desk rejection". The ECPR infographics print the top three submitting countries as Germany 15%, UK 9%, Netherlands 8% for 2024 and Germany 14%, UK 12%, USA 8% for 2023 |
| **Editorial-board geography** | 30 entries on the live page (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/european-journal-of-political-research/information/editorial-board, retrieved 2026-11-23): editor-in-chief 1 (The Netherlands); editors 5 (Germany, France, Belgium, Japan, Austria, one each); open-science editors 2 (Austria, Germany); editorial coordinator 1 (UK, ECPR staff); editorial board 21 (Germany 6, France 3, United Kingdom 3, Italy 2, Sweden 2, and one each in The Netherlands, United States, Australia, Belgium and Denmark). Totals: Germany 8, France 4, United Kingdom 4, The Netherlands 2, Belgium 2, Austria 2, Italy 2, Sweden 2, Japan 1, United States 1, Australia 1, Denmark 1 (8+4+4+2+2+2+2+2+1+1+1+1 = 30) |
| **Non-Western epistemology openness** | Keyword counts in the 555 records with abstracts: colonial or Indigenous terms 1 (0.2%); China, Chinese, Taiwan or Hong Kong 1 (0.2%); Israel, Palestine or Gaza 6 (1.1%). The editors call the journal "not limited to research on Europe" and encourage cases from outside Western Europe and from Central and Eastern Europe (editorial). No statement on non-Western epistemologies was found |
| **Diversity topic receptiveness** | Gender, women or feminism terms 60 (10.8%); race, racial, ethnic or minority terms 34 (6.1%); LGBT, queer, transgender or same-sex terms 10 (1.8%). The 2026 editorial has a diversity section reporting author-gender shares (at least one woman among the authors on just under 45% of submissions; all-male teams 35% against all-female 12% in 2025) and a stated aim of a more open, kind and diverse political science; the society's infographics print 33% female published authors for 2024 and 30% for 2023 |
| **Dominant theoretical tradition** | No tradition is stated; the aims text says the journal embraces all major subfields and methodological approaches, and research articles must situate empirical findings in existing theoretical debates (about and preparing-your-materials pages). By keyword counts, survey, experimental and causal-identification designs lead; normative or political-theory terms appear in 3.1%; interpretive, hermeneutic, genealogical or poststructural terms in 1 of 555. The six most-cited 2021-2026 items in Crossref (citation counts at retrieval) are: effect of COVID-19 lockdowns on political support (479; https://doi.org/10.1111/1475-6765.12401), political trust during the pandemic (259; https://doi.org/10.1111/1475-6765.12425), the coronavirus crisis and citizen trust (244; https://doi.org/10.1111/1475-6765.12419), partisan support for democratic backsliding (125; https://doi.org/10.1111/1475-6765.12502), governance-driven democratisation (98; https://doi.org/10.1111/1475-6765.12421), and stability and change in political trust across six panel studies (92; https://doi.org/10.1111/1475-6765.12606). The journal states no political position on any page read |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** Yes, stated: research articles "must situate empirical findings within existing theoretical and scholarly debates" and should show how the research "advances, challenges, or refines the current literature" and contribute to theory-building or theoretical innovation (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/european-journal-of-political-research/information/author-instructions/preparing-your-materials, retrieved 2026-11-23). The journal "strives to publish substantive scholarly contributions that go beyond presenting incremental evidence" (same page).
- **What kind of engagement?** Empirical political science of any subfield and any geographic area, quantitative, qualitative or mixed; normative political theory if it contributes to debates in empirical political science; review articles only with a substantive empirical contribution such as a systematic meta-analysis (same page). Research Notes make "a more focused and narrow contribution" with novel evidence or perspectives.
- **Article type and length**: Research Article up to 10,000 words and Research Note up to 5,000, both counting footnotes, tables and figures, with an abstract of up to 250 words and up to five keywords (same page).
- **Case-study framing**: "'topic X has never been studied in country Y' is insufficient" unless it comes with a clear theoretical or empirical articulation of what existing research gains (editorial, 2026-11-09, https://doi.org/10.1017/S1475676526101960).
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: the editors say desk rejection "is a very common occurrence ... the statistical mode", that authors of desk-rejected manuscripts are promised a substantive justification and suggestions, and that articles need a clear theoretical or empirical contribution to be sent out for review (editorial). The latest SciRev review shown (1 of 15; its year is not printed) reports a desk rejection saying the work did not engage closely enough with the generalist political science audience of the journal (https://scirev.org/reviews/european-journal-of-political-research/); a single anecdote.

### Methodological Preferences

> Counts are Crossref records of this journal dated 2021-01-01 to 2026-11-23 (591 journal-article records; 555 with an abstract) whose title or abstract matches the regex listed under AI-Research Notes. Shares use 555 as the denominator. Scoring convention of this research pass (its own, not an external standard): share 0 = 0; under 1% = 1; 1-5% = 2; over 5% = 3; a 4-5 only with a cited editorial statement. Scores measure how often a method appears, not how a reviewer would judge it. No 4-5 is assigned: the journal's text welcomes quantitative, qualitative and mixed methods without ranking them (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/european-journal-of-political-research/information/author-instructions/preparing-your-materials). Rows for political-science practice are added where the schema's rows do not fit.

| Method | Receptiveness (0-5) | Evidence |
|--------|---------------------|----------|
| Quantitative experimental | 3 | Experiment, randomized, field-experiment or survey-experiment terms 135 (24.3%) of 555 (regex `experiment`). The journal "encourages submitting authors to use preregistrations and pre-analysis plans whenever possible" (about page) and the editors say they will encourage pre-registration for hypothesis-testing research with new data (editorial); pre-registration terms appear in 17 records (3.1%, regex `preregistration`) |
| Quantitative observational / causal inference (added row) | 3 | Causal-identification terms 44 (7.9%) (regex `causal_identification`); survey, panel-data, cross-national or public-opinion terms 274 (49.4%) (regex `survey_data`). Authors of accepted articles must submit a reproducibility package to the EJPR Dataverse (research-transparency page, https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/european-journal-of-political-research/information/journal-policies/research-transparency) |
| Qualitative interviews | 2 | `interviews?` 12 (2.2%), the word "qualitative" 15 (2.7%) of 555. The transparency guidelines say they apply to quantitative and qualitative research and allow exemption requests (research-transparency page) |
| Qualitative case studies (added row) | 2 | Case-study, process-tracing, comparative-historical or within-case terms 11 (2.0%) (regex `case_study`). The editors say a single-country case needs an explicit theoretical or empirical articulation (editorial) |
| Autoethnography | 0 | Does not fit political science as a named method: 0 of 555 records match `auto-?ethnograph`, and 0 match `ethnograph`. The row is kept for schema parity |
| Theoretical / Conceptual (normative theory) | 2 | Normative, political-theory, political-philosophy, democratic-theory or theories-of-justice terms 17 (3.1%) (regex `normative_theory`). The instructions accept normative political theory that contributes to and challenges key debates in empirical political science (preparing-your-materials page); "Political Theory and Democracy" is the primary topic of 37 works (OpenAlex, 2021-2026) |
| Formal theory (added row) | 1 | Formal-model, formal-theory, game-theory, equilibrium, signaling-game, bargaining-model or theoretical-model terms 5 (0.9%) (regex `formal_model`; narrow, so a lower bound). No statement about formal theory was found on the pages read |
| Mixed methods | 1 | Mixed-methods, multimethod or nested-analysis terms 3 (0.5%) (regex `mixed_methods`); the instructions name mixed methods as acceptable |
| Meta-analysis / systematic review | 1 | Meta-analysis or systematic-review terms 3 (0.5%) of 555 (regex `meta_sr_only`). The instructions mention a "systematic meta-analysis" as a qualifying empirical contribution for a review article (preparing-your-materials page) |

### Voice & Style

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **First-person voice acceptance (0-5)** | Not scored. Of the 555 Crossref records with an abstract (2021-01-01 to 2026-11-23), 510 (91.9%) contain I, we, my or our (case-sensitive regex `\b(?:I|we|my|our|We|My|Our)\b`; retrieved 2026-11-23). Of the ten most recently dated records with abstracts (2026-10-01 to 2026-11-06, e.g. https://doi.org/10.1017/s1475676526101972, https://doi.org/10.1017/s1475676526101832, https://doi.org/10.1017/s1475676526101923), nine contain a first-person word. The instructions state no first-person rule |
| **Expected density** | Research articles up to 10,000 words and research notes up to 5,000 including footnotes, tables and figures (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/european-journal-of-political-research/information/author-instructions/preparing-your-materials, retrieved 2026-11-23). Abstract up to 250 words; median 172 in the Crossref sample |
| **Abstract and keywords** | Abstract of up to 250 words and up to five keywords (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/european-journal-of-political-research/information/author-instructions/preparing-your-materials, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Writing style notes** | Double-spaced with page numbers, 12 pt or larger, British or American English consistently, ECPR house style; Harvard author-date references (last name, year) with initials; any consistent referencing style is accepted at first submission (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/european-journal-of-political-research/information/author-instructions/preparing-your-materials, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Authorship pattern** | Crossref author lists for 567 of the 591 records: 1 author 128 (22.6%), 2 authors 203, 3 authors 141, 4 or more 95 (128+203+141+95 = 567). The 2026 editorial reports that the average number of authors per submitted article has risen over the past decade (https://doi.org/10.1017/S1475676526101960). Retrieved 2026-11-23 |

### Reviewer Pool Characteristics

Reviewer behaviour itself is not observable from public pages; what follows is what public pages, the editors' own report and SciRev show.

| Aspect | Detail | Evidence |
|--------|--------|----------|
| **Dominant tradition** | The board page lists names and affiliations but not disciplines or methods, so no methodological split can be counted. Structure (live page, retrieved 2026-11-23): 1 editor-in-chief, 5 editors, 2 open-science editors, 1 editorial coordinator, 21 editorial-board members (1+5+2+1+21 = 30). The society's infographics print 23 editorial-board members (48% female) for 2024 and 29 (51% female) for 2023 | https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/european-journal-of-political-research/information/editorial-board ; ECPR infographics (URLs in Metrics) |
| **Reviewer list size** | No separate reviewer list found on the pages read. Process: the aim is three reviews per submission (SciRev average over 15 reviews: 2.5 reports); editors may decide on fewer reviews if comments are clear and converging and the process has been excessively long (editorial) | https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/european-journal-of-political-research/information/peer-review-information/review-process ; https://doi.org/10.1017/S1475676526101960 ; https://scirev.org/journal/european-journal-of-political-research/ |
| **Review model** | Double-anonymous (review-process page) | https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/european-journal-of-political-research/information/peer-review-information/review-process |
| **Reviewer competence variance** | Blank. ### Practical Concerns

| Concern | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| **IRB requirement strictness** | A funding statement and a competing-interests statement are required in the submission; an ethical-standards statement is required if the work involves human subjects (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/european-journal-of-political-research/information/author-instructions/preparing-your-materials, retrieved 2026-11-23). The pages read do not specify an ethics-committee approval rule beyond that statement |
| **Single-author acceptance** | Single-author records are 128 of 567 Crossref records with author lists (22.6%) for 2021-2026 (retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Independent scholar friendliness** | Blank. The affiliation rule says affiliations should be the institution(s) at which the research was conducted, supported or approved; nothing on independent scholars (preparing-your-materials page, retrieved 2026-11-23; searched the instruction pages for "independent" and "unaffiliated" with no match) |
| **Data transparency requirement** | Required after conditional acceptance: a reproducibility package (README, clean data and documentation, code, output) goes to the EJPR Dataverse on Harvard Dataverse and the final manuscript carries a Data Availability Statement with the package's DOI; authors confirm compliance at submission and may request an exemption at that time; "Data available upon request" is not accepted (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/european-journal-of-political-research/information/journal-policies/research-transparency, retrieved 2026-11-23). Only the required procedures are mandatory |
| **OPSEC compatibility** | Double-anonymous; authors must remove identifying references, thanks and links to own websites or funded projects, keep self-citations to a minimum, avoid self-citing works in progress, and change the titles of papers presented at seminars or conferences (preparing-your-materials page, retrieved 2026-11-23). Preprints may be posted at any time (open-access-options page), which can reveal authorship |
| **AI use** | Disclosure required for generative use that produces text or images or analyses data; AI cannot be an author; reviewers must not upload manuscripts to AI tools (preparing-your-materials page and editorial, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Open access and cost** | Fully open access; APC GBP 2,610 or USD 3,655, with institutional agreements, equity schemes, waivers and discounts (fees-and-pricing and open-access-options pages, retrieved 2026-11-23) |

## Strategic Notes

> Each statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Where the evidence does not support a statement, the field says so.

### Hard Blockers

- **Length**: research articles up to 10,000 words and research notes up to 5,000 including footnotes, tables and figures; over-length manuscripts are returned and "we do not make exceptions" (Format).
- **Contribution to the literature**: the journal expects findings to be situated in theoretical debates and to go beyond incremental evidence; a case-only contribution does not pass desk review (Framing Requirements; editorial).
- **Anonymity**: identifying references, thanks, project links and self-citations to work in progress must be removed (Practical Concerns; preparing-your-materials page).
- **Data and code**: a reproducibility package must be submitted after conditional acceptance unless an exemption was requested at submission (Data transparency requirement).
- **AI use**: undeclared AI assistance in drafting "may lead to disqualification of the paper" (AI Policy).

### Soft Tax

- **Selectivity**: the editors call desk rejection the statistical mode; the society's infographics print a 65% "rejection rate" for 2024 and 533 submissions against 94 published articles (Metrics).
- **Time**: society-reported averages of 67 days to first editorial decision (2024) and 50 days from acceptance to publication; SciRev (n = 15) lists 5.3 months total for accepted manuscripts (Review Cycle Time).
- **Revision rounds**: one chance at a major revision; a second round of major revisions is "very exceptional" and reviewer scepticism after revision likely leads to rejection (Peer Review).
- **Cost**: Gold OA is the only route; the APC is GBP 2,610 or USD 3,655 unless an institutional agreement, equity scheme, waiver or discount applies (Open Access).
- **Preprints and anonymity**: preprints are allowed at any time but can reveal authorship under double-anonymous review (Preprint Policy).

### Best Suited For

- Comparative or behavioural empirical work, quantitative, qualitative or mixed, with a theoretical contribution: survey, experiment and causal terms in 49.4%, 24.3% and 7.9% of 555 abstracts; the editors stress contribution over site (Methodological Preferences; editorial).
- Work from outside Western and Northern Europe: the editors say they "strongly encourage" it and that the journal is not limited to Europe (Epistemological & Political Leanings).
- Pre-registered or open-science-oriented studies: the journal encourages pre-registration and has two open-science editors (Methodological Preferences; Identity).
- Open-access publication with funding routes: fully Gold OA with institutional, equity and waiver routes (Open Access).

### Not Recommended For

- Single-country descriptive work without a theoretical or empirical articulation: "topic X has never been studied in country Y" is not enough (Framing Requirements).
- Manuscripts over 10,000 words (or notes over 5,000): returned without exception (Format).
- Authors who need several revision rounds: the editors aim to decide after one round of revisions (Peer Review).
- Authors who cannot share data and code and have not requested an exemption at submission (Practical Concerns).
